spec.summary: Wishlist v1 has no matching event in the catalog, so this spec adds two new events: wishlist_item_added and wishlist_item_removed. Both are keyed on product_id (SKU), the same as product_viewed and product_added_to_cart, so saves can be joined to product data. Usage ('how many people') comes from distinct users firing wishlist_item_added. 'Which products' comes from counting by product_id and category, net of removals. Only new events are added and no existing event or property changes, so no existing KPI's numbers change. If the wishlist page later adds a 'move to cart' button, that would extend product_added_to_cart and affect add_to_cart_rate (see questions).
clarifying_questions: Can users add to cart directly from the wishlist page in v1? If so, product_added_to_cart needs a new optional source value 'wishlist'. That would affect add_to_cart_rate (owner: growth), because those adds have no preceding product_viewed on /p/*.
Where can users tap save in v1: only the product page, or also search results and recommendation carousels? This fixes the allowed values for source.
Should adoption be reported against signed-in users only (the eligible base), or against all users?

events.name: wishlist_item_added
events.trigger: Fires once when the server confirms a product was saved to the signed-in user's wishlist. Do not fire on the tap itself, on failure, or if the product was already in the wishlist. If a signed-out user taps save and is sent to sign in, fire only after the save completes after sign-in.
events.description: A signed-in user saved a product to their wishlist.

properties.name: product_id
properties.description: SKU of the saved product. Same format as product_viewed.product_id.

properties.name: category
properties.description: Product category. Same values as product_viewed.category.

properties.name: source
properties.description: Where the save happened. Mirrors product_added_to_cart.source.

events.name: wishlist_item_removed
events.trigger: Fires once when the server confirms a product was removed from the signed-in user's wishlist. Do not fire on failure or if the product was not in the wishlist. Do not fire when an item leaves the wishlist automatically, for example because the product was discontinued.
events.description: A signed-in user removed a product from their wishlist.

properties.name: product_id
properties.description: SKU of the removed product. Same format as product_viewed.product_id.

properties.name: category
properties.description: Product category. Same values as product_viewed.category.

properties.name: source
properties.description: Where the removal happened: the product page (unsaving) or the wishlist page.

spec.privacy_notes: Do not put email, name, phone or address in event properties. Identify the user only through the existing pseudonymous analytics user id set by the SDK at sign-in. Product SKU and category are not personal data. If wishlists later support names, notes or sharing, do not send free-text names or notes, or recipient details, in these events.
